what: Monster Beverage sells energy drinks. It develops and markets the brands, and Coca-Cola's bottlers handle most of the distribution. Monster Energy is its main brand, alongside Reign, Bang and the Monster Brewing alcohol range.
customers: Consumers buying from convenience stores, supermarkets and online; distribution runs mainly through Coca-Cola bottlers.
money: Monster Energy and its many variants
energy brands acquired from Coca-Cola such as NOS and Full Throttle
craft beer and flavoured malt beverages
moat: Brand strength in a category where shelf space is contested, plus access to the Coca-Cola bottling system, which a new entrant cannot buy.
risks: Celsius and newer brands have taken share in the United States
Regulators periodically examine caffeine content and marketing to young people
The alcohol business has performed poorly and has been written down
Aluminium and ingredient costs affect margins
opportunities: It carries no debt and about $3.7 billion of cash
International markets are still under-penetrated compared with the US
Price increases have held and gross margins have recovered
watch: US convenience store scanner data for Monster's market share against Celsius and Red Bull.
